title: tsx path-alias resolution (@/lib/...) depends on process.cwd(), fails silently from the wrong directory
summary: tsx's resolveTsPaths reads tsconfig.json path aliases relative to process.cwd() at launch, not the script's own location -- a Claude Code MCP server launched without the correct working directory fails alias imports like @/mcp/human-estimator/... even though the file exists. Fixed with a bash -c "cd <repo> && exec node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs <script>" wrapper (the leading ./ on --import matters: without it Node treats it as a bare specifier and throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND).
retrievalQuestions: Why does a tsx-loaded MCP server fail to resolve @/lib path aliases even though the file exists on disk?
What is the exact shell wrapper pattern for launching a tsx-based Claude Code MCP server from the correct working directory?
Why does node --import node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs fail with ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND while --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs works?

futureAgentInstructions.whenThisAppears: A Claude Code stdio MCP server built with TypeScript + tsx + tsconfig path aliases fails with module-not-found errors specifically on @/... imports
startAt: ~/.claude.json mcpServers entry for the affected server
doNot: Use --import node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs without a leading ./ or / -- Node treats it as a bare module specifier and throws ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND: Cannot find package 'node_modules'
Assume a tsx alias-resolution failure is a code bug in the imported file before checking the launch working directory
proveBeforeClaiming: The fixed command is bash -c "cd <repo> && exec node --import ./node_modules/tsx/dist/loader.mjs <script>"
A real tools/call against the previously-failing tool succeeds after the wrapper is applied, verified via claude mcp list and a direct MCP protocol probe
